clinician.trajectory_summary: A 52-year-old male presented to the emergency department with right lower quadrant abdominal pain. Initial examination revealed the patient to be afebrile and hypertensive with RLQ tenderness. CT abdomen/pelvis without contrast on admission identified acute appendicitis and an incidental right renal pole mass (8.0 x 6.9 x 7.1 cm), which was further characterized on MRI as an 8.4-cm heterogeneous renal mass with hypo-enhancing capsule. The patient underwent surgery (appendectomy). In the immediate postoperative period on Day 1, he developed hypoxia requiring supplemental oxygen with tachypnea and dyspnea with exertion. Despite the absence of classic PE symptoms at initial presentation, prior hemodynamic compromise, or positive venous Doppler findings, imaging obtained to evaluate the postoperative hypoxia and dyspnea revealed a massive saddle pulmonary embolism.
